canonical_policy.name: Default validation/logging
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: FluentValidation is the standard explicit request/use-case validation library; application logging uses ILogger<T> with Serilog as provider.

reviews.boundary_analysis: FluentValidation and ILogger/Serilog match; registration package and legacy automatic-integration exception versus hard checker error alreadyreplicaEXTRA0018/0009. No new blanket ban.

context_quotes: - Use FluentValidation for explicit request and use-case validation where appropriate, and keep each concern at its owning boundary: API validates transport and request-contract concerns, Application enforces use-case and straightforward workflow rules, Domain protects non-trivial invariants it genuinely owns, Infrastructure validates assumptions about external systems. Do not move Domain invariants into FluentValidation merely because the library is available, and do not duplicate the same rule mechanically at every layer.

- Default: `ILogger<T>` with structured message templates and stable property names; avoid string interpolation that turns structured values into opaque text.
- Default: when Serilog is configured, use the DI-integrated `AddSerilog` approach with provider configuration in environment-aware configuration; application code keeps depending on `ILogger<T>`.

- **Resilience** — when resilience is required, prefer `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` for HttpClient and `Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience` for general pipelines (D-12). Do not add the deprecated `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly` or `Polly.Extensions.Http`; a direct Polly reference or Polly API configuration is an explicit exception that needs a documented reason why the Microsoft.Extensions APIs cannot express the requirement.
- **API versioning** — when Controller API versioning has been explicitly adopted (D-15), use the Controller integration of `Asp.Versioning` (for example `Asp.Versioning.Mvc` with `Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer`); do not add it before the project actually adopts versioning.
- **Validation** — `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions` for registration; do not add a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement (D-05).

With `[ApiController]`, ASP.NET Core handles model-binding failures and can produce validation problem responses. FluentValidation expresses explicit rules for required business/application input, string or collection constraints, ranges, cross-property and conditional validation, and other request or use-case rules that read better as validators.

```text
API transport / request-contract concern       -> API boundary validation
Application use-case input or workflow rule    -> Application validator / Application Service
Non-trivial invariant genuinely owned by Domain -> Domain model
```

Register validators with `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions`, follow the project's established invocation pattern instead of adding a second competing mechanism, and avoid deprecated automatic-validation integration packages. A request can be syntactically valid and still violate an Application or Domain rule; when a rule is enforced in several layers, each layer has its own reason.

Raw exception messages or inconsistent anonymous error objects returned to clients; Application depending on HTTP status codes; every method returning `Result<T>`; exceptions for every negative branch; swallowed exceptions; catch/log/rethrow at every layer; the same failure logged repeatedly; sensitive details in `ProblemDetails`; business rules only in request validators; validation coupled to Minimal API endpoint filters in a Controller-based project.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Invalid HTTP input | Validation problem response |
| Simple query not found | Application returns `null`; API maps to `404` |
| Several expected business outcomes | Typed outcome or Result |
| Unexpected exception | Global `IExceptionHandler` |
| API failure contract | `ProblemDetails` |
| Straightforward use-case/workflow rule | Application validator / Application Service |
| Non-trivial invariant owned by Domain | Domain enforcement |
| Recoverable external failure | Handle or translate at the boundary |
| Unrecoverable external failure | Propagate to centralized handling |
| Client cancellation | Propagate; not a generic `500` |

Avoid interpolation, which turns structured values into opaque text and allocates even when the level is disabled:

Keep property names stable so logs stay queryable.

String interpolation in log calls; duplicate exception logging; expected outcomes logged as errors; credentials or secrets in logs; whole objects dumped without review; provider-specific APIs spread through Application code; logs used as an audit database without a dedicated audit design.

| Scenario | Technique |
|---|---|
| Application logging API | `ILogger<T>` |
| Context shared across log entries | `BeginScope` |
| Unexpected handled exception | Log once at the handling boundary |
| Expected business rejection | No Error log |
| Serilog setup, sinks, enrichers | `references/serilog.md` |
| High-volume measured hot path | `LoggerMessage` source generator |
The `Serilog.Sinks.Elasticsearch` package is deprecated; use the official `Elastic.Serilog.Sinks` package (same `WriteTo.Elasticsearch` name, ECS documents to data streams):

- `DTOs` — Application-level operation/data models when useful; not a dumping ground.
- `Validation` — FluentValidation validators for Application-level input and use-case validation.
- `DependencyInjection.cs` — registers Application services and Application-level validation infrastructure, never concrete Infrastructure implementations.

canonical_policy.name: Conditional mapping/resilience
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Manual mapping is fine for simple cases; Mapster is approved when mapping volume warrants it. Microsoft resilience packages are approved only when real integrations need resilience.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Manual simple mapping, conditional Mapster/resilience match. DI package couplingBF0080 and no hypothetical installation already covered.

context_quotes:
- Domain must stay independent of EF Core, ASP.NET Core, HTTP, persistence and external-service implementation concerns, including mapping-library concerns.
- Default: simple domain entities; CRUD-oriented and straightforward workflow rules belong in Application Services. Validation rules, immutable fields, status transitions or allowed/forbidden edits do not by themselves justify a Rich Domain Model.

- Add a dependency only for a concrete current requirement; do not install packages for hypothetical future use. An approved conditional technology is added only when its capability is actually needed.

1. Confirm a concrete current requirement (`rules/common/dependencies.md` § Need).
2. Use the approved technology from the decision register; a conditional technology only when its capability is now needed. A new major library or framework, or a replacement of an approved technology, is Reserved — stop with a Decision Request (CLAUDE.md § Decisions).
3. Apply the package-specific choices below.
Azure Key Vault is one possible managed provider — add Azure-specific packages only when the project actually runs on Azure:

Add only the infrastructure the project actually uses — not PostgreSQL, Redis or RabbitMQ because they are common in examples — and keep local passwords in an ignored `.env` or similar developer configuration.

SDK image as production runtime; root execution without reason; secrets baked into images; arbitrary infrastructure in Compose; assuming `curl`/`wget` exist; production migrations at application startup (see also: `delivery-pipeline` § 3); specialized image variants without compatibility checks; Docker concerns leaking into Domain/Application code.

Resilience policies match failure and operation semantics; add a mechanism only for an identified failure scenario, and observe retries, timeouts and circuit state when they matter operationally. The Microsoft packages are built on Polly v8, but application code uses the `Microsoft.Extensions` resilience APIs.

The standard handler is useful when its behavior fits the remote API; it is not mandatory for every client. Review its retry behavior carefully for state-changing requests, and avoid stacking handlers with overlapping strategies.

Useful signals: retry counts, timeout frequency, circuit state, rate-limit rejections, dependency latency. Use the telemetry stack the project adopted; resilience handlers alone do not justify adding OpenTelemetry.

Keep levels, sinks and overrides in configuration so they can differ per environment. The example shows several optional sinks at once — File, Seq and others are not baseline dependencies; a Console sink suffices for a simple local Development baseline, and numeric limits and retention values are illustrative.

1. **Determine scope.** Decide what the request needs: backend, Angular frontend, test projects, documentation, external integrations, mapping, containerization. Do not scaffold optional infrastructure because it may be useful later.
2. **Read the decisions.** Use the decided stack; conditional technologies only when the project needs their capability now.
3. **Repository-level structure.** Create only the required top-level directories and repository-wide files (`references/solution-layout.md`): `.slnx`, `Directory.Build.props`, `Directory.Packages.props`, `global.json`, `.editorconfig`, `.gitignore`, `README.md`.

- `Abstractions/ExternalServices` — Application-owned abstractions implemented by outer layers: `IEmailSender.cs`, `ICurrentUser.cs`, `IFileStorage.cs`, `IPaymentGateway.cs`. Create it when such a dependency exists.
- `Services` — Application Services and useful public service contracts: `ITaskService.cs`, `TaskService.cs`. No handler, CQRS or MediatR structures.
- `DTOs` — Application-level operation/data models when useful; not a dumping ground.

context_quotes: Useful targets: meaningful component behavior, validation, data-access request mapping, important route/auth behavior, complex reactive state — not Angular framework internals. Run the workspace's configured test runner. E2E tests cover a small number of important user workflows unless the project requires more, and the same behavior is not duplicated at every level.

6. **Packages.** Add each baseline package through `add-dependency` (`references/baseline-setup.md`); resolve versions at install time and never copy versions from examples.
7. **Test projects.** Create only useful test projects beside production projects under `backend/` (typically `Application.Tests` and `IntegrationTests`; `Domain.Tests` only when Domain has non-trivial behavior; `Infrastructure.Tests` only for a concrete need). Angular unit/component tests stay in the Angular workspace; E2E tests, when adopted, under `frontend/<Name>.Web/e2e/`.
8. **Angular application.** When frontend scope exists, create the workspace under `frontend/<Name>.Web/` with the Angular CLI and the decided frontend options (`references/baseline-setup.md`). Frontend structure: `rules/frontend/angular.md`.

Use the latest stable Angular release supported by the selected Node.js environment and create the workspace with the current Angular CLI so that it selects mutually compatible Angular, TypeScript and RxJS versions — do not upgrade TypeScript beyond Angular's supported range independently. Select standalone APIs, strict mode, routing, SCSS and zoneless mode when the selected stable version supports it; add Angular Material and CDK with the Angular CLI. Configure the decided unit-test runner (D-09); add E2E tooling only under D-13.

Angular unit and component tests stay in the workspace, usually colocated with the code they test. E2E tests, when adopted, also stay in the workspace, for example `frontend/ProjectName.Web/e2e/`. Angular tests never go under `backend/`.

canonical_policy.name: API versioning package is conditional
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: When Controller API versioning is explicitly adopted, use the Controller integration of Asp.Versioning; do not add the package before the project actually adopts versioning.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Adopted Controller integration only matches; explicit adoptionReserved alreadyEXTRA0008. ExamplesMvc/ApiExplorer not new blanket versions.

context_quotes:
- **Resilience** — when resilience is required, prefer `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience` for HttpClient and `Microsoft.Extensions.Resilience` for general pipelines (D-12). Do not add the deprecated `Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly` or `Polly.Extensions.Http`; a direct Polly reference or Polly API configuration is an explicit exception that needs a documented reason why the Microsoft.Extensions APIs cannot express the requirement.
- **API versioning** — when Controller API versioning has been explicitly adopted (D-15), use the Controller integration of `Asp.Versioning` (for example `Asp.Versioning.Mvc` with `Asp.Versioning.Mvc.ApiExplorer`); do not add it before the project actually adopts versioning.
- **Validation** — `FluentValidation.DependencyInjectionExtensions` for registration; do not add a deprecated or legacy ASP.NET automatic-validation integration package without a concrete requirement (D-05).
Rules: `rules/backend/api.md` § Versioning. Decision: D-15 (adopting versioning is Reserved).

canonical_policy.name: Docker is optional infrastructure
canonical_policy.normalized_policy: Do not introduce Docker merely because the application can be containerized; add container artifacts only when the project or deployment actually needs them.

reviews.boundary_analysis: Optional actual deployment/container need matches. CIpublish gate, Composeactualinfra, AngularNodebuild and Nginxnotmandatory/configcompatibility already separately covered.

context_quotes: Angular artifacts come from `npm run build`. Store or publish only artifacts that later stages need. Build and publish container images from CI only when container deployment is part of the project.

Project-specific database infrastructure in a generic pipeline; deployment secrets in YAML; different source rebuilt per environment without reason; failing tests suppressed to allow deployment; automatic production seeding or startup migrations; assumed Docker deployment; assumed frontend scripts.

Containers are optional (D-14). Technique: `ci-cd` (pipeline shapes, artifacts, secrets) and `docker` (images, Compose, probes). Container image rules: `rules/backend/hosting.md`; secrets: `rules/common/security.md`.

Inspect what actually exists before writing anything: .NET backend, Angular frontend, test projects, Dockerfiles, provider-specific integration tests, generated clients, deployment artifacts. Do not assume PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker or frontend tooling exists; add stages for the actual project, not generic boilerplate. Introduce Docker or container publishing only when the project has adopted containers.

Rules: `rules/backend/hosting.md` § Containers, `rules/common/security.md` § Secrets. Decision: D-14 (containers are optional). Workflow: `delivery-pipeline` (container and deployment changes).

Keep build tooling out of production runtime images, configuration external, images reproducible and Docker concerns out of the application architecture; prefer the deployment platform's health-probe capabilities.

Copy only the repository-level build files that exist and restore needs, and copy project files explicitly — wildcard tricks can flatten or rearrange the multi-project structure. Use the .NET runtime image (not `aspnet`) for workers that do not need ASP.NET Core.

## Restore caching

Copy project and build files before the full source so source changes do not invalidate the NuGet restore layer. When the solution structure changes, update the project-copy section; a correct restore graph matters more than layer caching.

Pass environment-specific configuration at runtime:

Add only the infrastructure the project actually uses — not PostgreSQL, Redis or RabbitMQ because they are common in examples — and keep local passwords in an ignored `.env` or similar developer configuration.

For a static Angular deployment, build in a Node stage and serve the generated assets with the chosen hosting strategy; Nginx is not mandatory when the platform hosts static files. Keep API base URLs and environment configuration compatible with that strategy.

SDK image as production runtime; root execution without reason; secrets baked into images; arbitrary infrastructure in Compose; assuming `curl`/`wget` exist; production migrations at application startup (see also: `delivery-pipeline` § 3); specialized image variants without compatibility checks; Docker concerns leaking into Domain/Application code.

1. **Determine scope.** Decide what the request needs: backend, Angular frontend, test projects, documentation, external integrations, mapping, containerization. Do not scaffold optional infrastructure because it may be useful later.
2. **Read the decisions.** Use the decided stack; conditional technologies only when the project needs their capability now.

MediatR, CQRS handler trees, Vertical Slice Architecture, Domain Events, Specifications, SharedKernel, BuildingBlocks, EventBus, messaging, microservices, Kubernetes, cloud-specific projects, state-management frameworks, Docker files and deployment manifests — each needs an actual requirement, and most are Reserved.
Docker files, deployment manifests, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, messaging infrastructure and additional services are introduced only for a concrete requirement.
